subject: A small red fox craftsperson with a sea-green scarf, a blue sketchbook and a golden pencil.
style: Detailed warm storybook fox: soft short fur, expressive eyes, tailored teal scarf and crafted props
prompt: Refine the existing orange-and-cream fox craftsperson into a premium, expressive, fully modeled storybook character. Preserve the teal scarf, navy sketchbook, gold pencil, twenty named joints and the four authored actions. Replace ball-separated arms and knees with continuous weighted skin; shape a broad-cheeked tapered face, cupped pointed ears, curved fluffy tail, glossy amber eyes with sclera, eyelids and small catchlights, a soft triangular nose and a subtle smile. Add short geometric fur and embedded procedural fur textures, cloth folds and scarf fringes, a bound book with page edges, elastic strap and cover emblem, and a real wood/graphite pencil tip. Use physically based opaque surfaces; preserve every visible detail in the animated GLB, not just the portrait. Author the back, underside, topology and skin weights explicitly; do not claim recovered anatomy or fur simulation.
authored_assumptions: This is a new authored 3D interpretation of the existing original fox design, not recovered geometry or a neural text-to-3D result.
Complete hidden surfaces and twenty-bone rest layout are authored; the original fox left/right bone names are preserved as identifiers.
The continuous arm and leg lofts use explicit multi-bone skin blends around elbows and knees; they are not muscle or cloth simulations.
Short fur is bounded opaque tapered triangle geometry attached with interpolated skin weights, plus embedded procedural albedo/normal textures. It is not a strand groom or dynamically simulated fur.
The scarf, eyelids, fingers and face are sculpted fixed geometry without independent expressions or cloth dynamics.
The book drawings and pencil strokes remain authored gestures: no new ink or page simulation is claimed.
This PBR browser-quality variant is separate from Weft's restricted diffuse-only importer profile.
The preserved four skeletal actions are authored animation, not learned behavior or Weft physics.

attachments.name: sketchbook
attachments.placement: Held against left paw, visible in front of chest.
attachments.authored_assumption: Rigid held prop; no page-turning simulation.

attachments.name: pencil
attachments.placement: Held diagonally in right paw toward sketchbook.
attachments.authored_assumption: Rigid tool; short wrist rotations convey drawing.

states.meaning: Quiet attentive breathing, alternating ear twitches and a slow tail sway.
Looks down at the sketchbook and draws a craft pattern with several short pencil strokes.
Raises both paws clearly above shoulder level, displaying the sketchbook and pencil during one delighted hop, then returns to rest.
Raises the sketchbook toward its face and reads it with a pronounced downward gaze and slow page scan; pencil hand stays resting.

source_prompt: Create an editable, controllable full-body stylized red fox craftsperson. Preserve the red-orange coat, cream muzzle/chest/tail tip, dark sock paws, oversized triangular ears, sea-green scarf, navy sketchbook, golden pencil and curled sweeping tail in every state. Author unseen surfaces consistently; this is an original toy-like 3D design, not a recovered scan. Idle should breathe and listen, making_something should sketch with repeated short pencil strokes, working should read the sketchbook with a slow gaze scan, and milestone_level_up should lift both tools and hop once. Keep the camera fixed and the whole body visible. Revision: keep the existing palette, face, proportions and camera. Close elbow and knee gaps with small smooth joints. For milestone_level_up, raise the shoulders and bend both forearms until paws and held tools are above shoulder height; include one gentle upward hop. Keep book facing the viewer at the peak. Further working-state refinement: visibly lift the book toward the face with the left arm, lower the gaze and scan the raised page. Keep the right pencil hand resting so reading and sketching are clearly different actions.
